caption:
Indiana mountain giant down! 

Hudson has been grinding all season long.  Started out glassing early summer velvet giants in Kentucky and with the temperatures being awful down here he decided to cross the river north and go try his luck up in Indiana on some new land and get after a couple Hoosier bucks! 

Hudson got up in an old wooden blind that evidently had not been hunted for a couple years and dropped this brute right in his tracks. Insane shot through a small opening only about the diameter of a basketball as he walked up the point towards Hudson. Shout out to Kyuss Gargett and family for helping us out! 

Time to fill that #kentucky tag now!!

caption:
Welcome to the team, @jacksonsoucie.

Jackson will be joining the staff at Velo Baseball this summer and again over the winter break to offer pitching training. A Velo athlete since day one—and the (more athletic) brother of founder @tyler.soucie—Jackson has spent a lifetime immersed in the game and is now ready to pass that knowledge on.

He enters his senior year with @kentuckybaseball in the SEC, the most competitive conference in college baseball.

His resume speaks for itself:
– 2022 Connie Mack World Series Champion
– 2022 MLB Draft League
– 2023 DI JUCO World Series National Runner-Up
– 2024 Canadian Baseball Network Player of the Year
– 2024 Region 24 Pitcher of the Year
– 2024 GRAC Pitcher of the Year
– 2024 All-GRAC Team
– 2024 All-Region Team

Jackson will be available for sessions from July 1st until mid-August, and again during December and January. Bookings open soon.

2025 STEPHEN STRASBURG TOP PRO PROSPECT🌟

Congratulations to Leighton Harris (@kentuckybaseball) of the @newportgulls!

caption:
Unexpectedely saying good-bye to my Dad wednesday morning was the hardest thing I have ever done. Words cannot decribe how much we loved him. My mom and him worked as hard as they possibly could to give us the best childhood they could. He was everything I could ever ask for. Never missed a ball-game, never missed a chance to tell me he was proud of me, and never once chose himself over our family. I wish he could have seen some Milwaukee baseball games, met his grandkids, been at my siblings future weddings, but ultimately I know he will be watching over all of us 24/7. I miss you so much already Dad, and I'm going to strive everyday to keep making you proud. 
Rest easy Pops❤️

athlete.name: Chase Alderman
athlete.bio: A fierce competitor with an arsenal of sharp pitches, this right-handed pitcher blends poise and intensity on the mound. Known for a strategic mindset, he thrives under pressure, inspiring teammates daily.

caption:
When I first met Chase as a freshman, he was as raw as it gets, just a ton of untapped potential. He came in at 185lbs and by the end of the year he was sitting at 205lbs. The weight and strength gain, coupled with his freakish mobility, allowed him to go from 92 to 98 in 8 months. Chase was selected to the All-ASUN Freshman team and was then able to transfer to the University of Kentucky.⁠
⁠
Chase’s story is proof that with consistency, guidance, and time, you can make the adjustments needed to reach another level. After overcoming an ACL injury last season, he’s set to play a huge role on the University of Kentucky’s pitching staff this year.⁠
⁠
Proud, but not surprised.

caption:
I've been getting a lot of questions so I wanted to just answer them publicly here to put it to rest. 

A couple weeks ago I had to make a really tough choice. I got an offer that would make me eligible for all ten regular season games but in return I had to give up the play offs. I love my team, I love this sport and I love winning but at the end of the day I want my legacy to be about more than what I can do for myself. So I took it. I took it because any kid in Ohio can now use my example to claim their full regular season eligibility. Sometimes I think people don't realize what football does for kids like us -- it changes our future, it's a home, it's a second family, it's something we build our lives on. And we give it EVERYTHING in return. No one should be taking that away from us. So yes, everything in me wishes I was gonna be on the field instead of on the sideline come playoffs. But sometimes you have to take a different kind of win and this is the one I wanted to leave behind -- for every student Athlete in Ohio that follows, you should know that if it is claimed that you have not complied with a bonafide exemption, you should be entitled to the same relief—to play a full season so you can be seen and have every opportunity to succeed. Love you all. BRob.

caption:
Great week with University of Kentucky, 5th year senior long snapper, Alex McLaughlin. 

Alex is a very impressive snapper who demonstrates great velocity, accuracy and consistency. Our focus during his visit was footwork and blocking transition. Already playing in a semi-pro style punt unit, Alex is required to block on every rep. We hammered footwork drills, implemented fast eyes, feet and hands, all while executing his snap and maintaining body control and solid pad level. He adapted like a vet to all drills and excelled. I hope he gained a lot of knowledge and some new tools to take into spring ball. It was an honor to help and I look forward to working with him this summer! Best off season yet! Stay Ready🤟

caption:
Kentucky long snapper David LaGanga has been trusting the process and continuously growing!

David and I met after his redshirt freshman year while he was at Lehigh. He was a backup and wanted to improve to take over the starting job. 

Needless to say, he definitely improved and went on to win the starting role and was named to the All Conference team back to back seasons!

David decided to make a change and is now at the University of Kentucky where he continues to train consistently with me and is growing daily. 

Crazy to see the changes when guys trust the process!

caption:
My walk with faith has been a long one, that really started about a little under 2 years ago. But even as I have been growing in my faith it has been a process, a continual decision every day to follow Jesus.

I had first wanted to get re-baptized/baptism of repentance earlier this year and God told me when I come out of that water all chains will be released, but it never happened. This weekend I got to face a lot of things since childhood, issues, and struggles that lingered until this day and after a group time of confession and conversation with close friends, God told me it was time. Time to come out of the water freed, chains released, in full surrender, ready to do something big, and a life decided to showing people the love of Christ.

Thank you God for loving a sinner like me, that even though I continually disobey… you still love me. Through that mercy is a call for response to it. I now see how important it is to be all in for Christ in everything. 

So today just know… things are about to change, I am all in, no more entertaining worldly things, I am a servant of God and there is nothing else I would rather be.

#godisgood #readyforrevival

caption:
Nobody can do the work for you.

If you want something, you can get it.

But you can’t wait for someone else to give it to you. You can’t wait for the sun to shine or for everything to be perfect - because it will never be.

Your goals are your responsibility and you’re the only one who can turn yourself into the person you need to be to achieve them.

You can have anything you want in life.

But you have to know what it is you want, and you have to be willing to become the type of person capable of getting it.

Nobody but you can do the work that matters - The work on yourself.

caption:
This week my sister and I lost our biggest fan, Hector Calzada Sr. As I step into my 7th year of college football, I can’t help but reflect on where my resilience truly comes from. Two grandparents who left everything behind and came to America in 1960, building a life from scratch so that their children and generations to come could have a shot. My sister and I are now living the dream that they had many years ago. 
My abuelo didn’t just lead with strength, he led with love. He served, supported, and sacrificed for his family in every way. My abuelitos’ (grandparents’) legacy lives on in all of us. The Calzada name will live FOREVER. Love you 🇨🇺🕊️

Florida’s Denzel Aberdeen has been one of the best backup guards in the whole nation right now

Denzel’s production goes far past the stat sheet itself but he’s been playing great as of late, averaging 9.3 PPG since their win against UVA, 2.4 APG and holding his opponents to a 25% FG percentage while he is shooting 40% from deep 

Yesterday he nearly led Florida in scoring with 16 points in only 20 minutes of play, while holding Tennessee’s star guard play to a total of 1-13 shooting against him

He’s a fantastic defender, high level athlete, leading Florida in assist to turnovers

When you’re playing behind an NBA Level backcourt it’s tough to get a ton of reps but he’s earned it and now producing at a high level.

athlete.bio: A tenacious forward from Kentucky, she blends agility with fierce determination, often leaving defenders in her wake. Off the field, her infectious energy and passion for teamwork inspire those around her.

caption:
Kaelyn earned all of this. I’ve had the privilege to be along her basketball journey and help her with her development, and when I tell you she’s been an All-American long before she was named one, I mean that her work ethic and what she does to get better has always matched what she says she’s gonna do and achieve.

With last year being a pivotal year for her, we sat down outside the gym in early spring with her mom to plan out the next year. We talked about Kaelyn’s goals, the 3 keys we would work on when on the court, blocking off time for her to do her strength & conditioning and recovery, who she would study on her own time and emulate parts of her game after, and what she would do personally to keep developing her mindset. 

While she was at school, when she was at home, or when she was traveling for AAU - all of her time to develop was planned within these schedules because when you want to be as great as Kaelyn does, you have to prioritize the things you need to do to get the things you want to get.

And Kaelyn has done everything we talked about on her plan, and she’s done it CONSISTENTLY. She’s never not done a film study when asked to. She’s never not shown up for a workout. She’s always early, always prepared, and always focused. Her massive goals are matched by her massive action and daily commitment to get better, and that’s why she accomplishes them. 

And through all of her success, she’s managed to be humble through it all, not letting any of the special experiences and accolades she’s achieved change up who she is and how she treats people. A special shoutout for a special person, I am so proud of you K! 💛🔒📈

caption:
First off, I want to give all glory to God. Without him I wouldn’t be where I am today and have the opportunities he has allowed me. Second, I want to thank my mom and dad for being my rocks through this whole process and constantly guiding me on and off the court to be the best version of myself. Along with my brother who has never left my corner and has supported me endlessly through everything. 
A big shout out to Coach Laurie Bollin for always believing in me, encouraging me to trust the process and hard work every day. I am so proud to have been part of the Bay State Jags family since 3rd grade! Many thanks and appreciation to all my coaches and trainers who have helped along my journey to grow as a player- Sam, Matt, Tiff, Nick, and Rocky. Also, thank you to my Tabor Academy Coaches Becker, Caputi, Conley and teammates for the love and support throughout High School. To my closest friends and family I’m so grateful to have you in my life. Without you all I wouldn’t be in this position today. 
And finally, I want to thank Coach Brooks and the entire Kentucky coaching staff for giving me this opportunity to live out my dreams and play at the next level. With that being said I would like to officially announce my commitment to the University of Kentucky! GO WILDCATS 💙

caption:
For my Senior Portfolio I decided to start a video podcast called Greater Than. This will drop on YouTube April 24th!  The whole purpose of this podcast is to highlight the fact that yes, we are athletes, you see our stats and we’re known for our accomplishments on the court, track, field, etc. but it’s only a morsel of who we are. This is a platform that we GET TO have the opportunity to share the love of our game and bring families and friends together to cheer on top of life’s trials and triumphs — Real G’s Know!

ON THIS EPISODE: 
All of the greats are people who refused to give up, even in the face of failure and adversity. You’ve seen her drive down the court every game, starting as a freshman as one of the most consistent players but what makes Asia Boone today? 
 Introducing Asia “The Sleeper” Boone, the Liberty Lady Flames guard who won NINE CUSA Freshman of the Week Honors in her career at Liberty University, shares her journey of how she started from the bench, shifted her anxiety and negative mindset to God— now, she starts for Liberty. Playing on multiple AAU teams, Asia did not know she would be recruited but she kept persevering on the court leading her right to greatness at Vines Center. 

@_asia.boone  beyond the court is a burst of joy, a woman of unwavering and great faith, a devoted friend, and an example of resilience. As she continues to develop in her career, may her journey serve as an inspiration to young, aspiring athletes worldwide who deal with anxiety or feel stuck and rely on their faith to push through.

Thanks for coming Asia!! Can’t wait to see how you continue to grow!

Music: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRhGiqP6YHM

(Highlights and reels compiled from @libertyflames)

caption:
The power of truly letting go and letting God!
•
The beginning of this year was one of the hardest times in my life. My mental health was struggling.
My life felt out of control. I was losing things that were so important to me and my question the whole time was why. Why is this happening to me? God, why am I going through this?

I realized that I was trying to control my own life and the weight of it all was too much for me to carry on my own. We are not made to carry any weight on our own.

I ended up truly letting go and letting God because I felt like I had nothing left to give. I couldn’t imagine the pain or stress ending, but it did! It took prayer and time for it to all turn around, but it did get better and it will get better.

By giving it to God, I didn’t need to worry or take control of everything because He has a plan for me and you and He WILL NOT fail us. He is not a God that fails. That is something I could trust.

I wouldn’t be where I am now without God. He has transformed my life for the better and I am eternally grateful to call Him my Lord and Savior!

We are not promised an easy life because we follow Jesus, but we are promised that every battle we face we will get through because of Him.

He will always meet you where you are. No one is too far gone.

Jesus loves you!

caption:
I did it.

They really mean it when you say you can do anything you put your mind to. I’ve had this goal for so many years and I’m so proud to say that I accomplished it! This definitely wasn’t an easy journey; I had so many injuries, countless mental blocks, and people that didn’t believe in me. However, I also had tons of motivation and passion which kept me fighting and pushing towards this huge dream, and ultimately, it led me to one of the best teams in the NCAA.

To all my coaches: no matter when you were a part of my story, thank you for training me to be the athlete I am today. You all play such significant roles in my time as a club gymnast, and I’m forever grateful for the time and effort you spent with me🫶

With all this said, I am so happy to announce my commitment to the University of Kentucky to continue my academic and athletic career!🥹 Tim, Rachel, and Chad, thank you so much for this incredible opportunity! I cannot wait to begin this beautiful and exciting chapter, it’s truly a dream come true💙

To everyone reading, never EVER give up on ideas that seem far fetched. Nothing is impossible. Go wildcats😼

caption:
I know I already posted these on my story, but these photos mean so much to me that I felt the need to put them on my feed:)
-
My relationship with gymnastics has never been simple. There have been endless times where I wanted to miss practice, endless times where I wanted to quit, and endless times where I wanted to give it all up. Yet to this day, there has always been this lingering, gut feeling that told me to keep fighting and pushing, and ultimately, it led me to pure happiness❤️ 

After not competing for almost 2 years, I got the opportunity to compete at my first level 10 meet. Now, I did fall, I didn’t hit my splits (sorry @aribeiro626😅), and I did wobble, but at the end of the day, I know I’ve come so far, and I know I will go farther. I know I will put in the work. I know I will succeed. 

I’m not done yet. Let the 2024-2025 season begin. #AAOWeFO❤️💙🤟

Last club meet is officially in the books!
Nationals 2025 ✅

What a way to end my club career! Just being here again after 3 surgeries in the last 3 years meant everything to me and was a win in my book. I could have given up, but I didn’t, and for that, I am so proud of myself. I’m so happy I was able to compete for Region 7 at Nationals one last time. I am forever and eternally grateful to God, my family, my coaches, my friends, my doctors, my PTs, and Excalibur, my gym home. I’m so excited for what life has in store for me next!

caption:
Yet not I, but through Christ in me. 

at the beginning of this preseason I made a goal to make gymnastics my mission field (thank you @jacibabbs). I wanted to use every opportunity God had blessed me with through this sport to glorify Him, in and out of the gym. gymnastics has been an idol for me for so long, and it was time for me to let it all go and lay it down at the feet of Jesus. I wasn’t working everyday for me anymore, I was working for the Lord and for the team He has so graciously blessed me with. I was working with a heart of gratitude, thankful every single day for the ability to get to do such a sport, knowing that I am made completely whole and not lacking anything in my identity as a child of God. I can’t take an ounce of credit for that moment I had prayed so long for that happened last night because God is the one who made it happen. HE is the one who deserves the glory because without Him, none of this would matter. so thank you Jesus for never ever leaving my side through any of it, for calling me by my name, for breathing breath into my lungs everyday, and for blessing me so so abundantly. 

“Now to Him who is able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine, according to His power that is at work within us, to Him be glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations for ever and ever! Amen.” Ephesians 3:20-21

caption:
I am overflowing with gratitude. THANK YOU JESUS for this amazing opportunity to be able to serve you and others in Honduras. 

There are so many emotions I am feeling after hearing the heart-wrenching stories of what these children and families go through every day. Despite having so little by the world’s standards, these children and families continue to show love, faith, and gratitude. I have witnessed that there can be joy in every moment, good or bad and the children’s smiles truly encompass that.

Some things that we were able to accomplish were taking 14 suitcases filled with medical supplies to help support the mamas and babies in the nicu, fulfilling a kids dream of one day having a bed, being able to supply seizure medicine to someone that wasn’t able to afford it, providing food so that the children were able to have meals, bringing a chair to a sweet girl with cerebral palsy, and helping out with the cost of surgery’s/procedures for families that couldn’t provide that for their children. There are so many more ways that God provided and led us this past week that I would LOVE to share❤️

This trip we prayed, laughed, cried, and saw God move in so many ways. I can’t wait to go back soon. This trip was a reminder to me that God is alive and He is so good. 

Thank you to everyone who prayed, encouraged, and supported us while on this journey. I am beyond grateful❤️And thank you Jackie for inviting me to come on this life changing trip, your love for Christ is shown every day through your actions and I am so grateful for you!

caption:
Here’s a full training day for the one and only @georgia.watsonnn ⬇️🏐

Georgia is in offseason mode and has 4 weeks until she is officially on campus as a Kentucky Wildcat

Here’s the full breakdown of Georgia’s training day:

Prep
-Warm up (not showcased)
-TRX ER holds 2 sets 5x5s hold
-Staggered Stance Rhythm Pogos 1x6 jumps each side
-Double hop bounds x20yd down & back
-Fast feet twitch drill x12s easier

Main Jumps:
-Sidestep to Hurdle 1x3 each side
-Single Leg Approach Jumps 1x3 each side
-Max Effort Approach (6 hurdles & Vertec Test)

Sprints
-5yd Build 10yd Fly x2 Reps
-10yd Build 10yd Fly x2 Reps

Lift:
-Pause Squats 4x3 Reps
-Pause Chin Ups 4x3 Reps
-DB Bench 4x6 Reps
-Seated Calf Raise 1x25-30

Recovery:

-Nasal Breathing x 10 Breaths (5 second inhale, 7 second exhale, 3 second hold)

Georgia is one of the most dedicated and hardworking athletes I have ever met, and is also one of the most elite humans as well

To all the folks at Kentucky, you guys will be lucky to have her, as she has been an honor to work with as an athlete the last few years 💪🏽

Give this workout a try if you want to become elite like our friend Georgia 🚀🏐

caption:
Coaching middle schoolers has reminded me that growth doesn’t always look perfect It looks like trying again, asking questions, celebrating small wins, and learning to trust yourself. I get a front-row seat to some of the most important years of their lives, and my goal is to give them a space where they feel valued, challenged, and proud of their progress. 

These kids show up with so much personality and potential, and watching them build confidence day by day is something I’ll never get tired of. Coaching them isn’t just about sports, it’s about helping them learn who they are. And I’m grateful for every minute. Watching their confidence build and seeing them accomplish things they didn’t believe they could… that’s the real victory. Grateful for this team and this journey. 

Thank you Mills Park Middle School Community and Coach Smith (pops) for allowing me kick off my first Season coaching and developing student athletes🫱🏽‍🫲🏾!

caption:
From Player to Leader: Ella Emmert on Navigating Collegiate Athletics

In this episode of the Contacts Coaching Podcast, we pivot from our usual focus on coaching to gain valuable insights from current collegiate athlete Ella Emmert, catcher at the University of Kentucky. Ella shares her unique journey into athletics, starting softball at age 10, and overcoming challenges to play at the collegiate level. She discusses the importance of gratitude, identity, and living in the present, all crucial components of her athletic and leadership success. Additionally, Ella gives us a behind-the-scenes look at her roles on multiple NCAA and SEC advisory committees, offering perspective on the evolving landscape of college sports. This conversation is a treasure trove of advice and inspiration for athletes, coaches, and anyone navigating competitive environments.

caption:
Speed doesn’t always = a better situation.
With adding tempo we have to understand that we are going to miss.. and sometimes shot commit our pin hitter.. this isn’t a big deal unless it’s obvious to opposing middle blocker and they have the visual cues to read and close.

If we’re in a control position, I think it’s important to add in a little deception, at the very minimum not giving any visual cues to where we are going to set.

With adding tempo, sometimes the worst sets can actually be the best set opening up a clear net - ie: inside set.

But if the set location was obvious from the start, the middle blocker is able to close, we are putting our pin hitter in a worse situation rather than just setting them a highball.

If you are a libero and looking to set with tempo, I believe it’s very important to get extra reps outside of team training - feeling confident before you start initiating them in team training. 

A libero who can keep the tempo after a settee dig will provide a ton of value for the team in transforming and I think we’re going see more and more liberos setting like @mollytuozzo in the next 5 years.

caption:
“You’re not on this team by accident.”

In Episode 2 of Beam Boldly with Brooke Gleichowski, Sharon Lee and Creslyn Brose share how shifting their mindset as college gymnasts changed everything — from competing for themselves to serving the people God placed around them.
This conversation reframes team culture in NCAA gymnastics through a faith-based lens. Instead of focusing only on lineups, scores, and individual performance, Sharon and Creslyn talk about asking a different question:
How does God want me to serve the people on this team right now?

Rooted in Esther 4:14 — “for such a time as this”, this moment is a reminder that every roster, every season, and every teammate is intentional. You are placed where purpose meets preparation — not just to compete, but to love, lead, and reflect Christ.

This episode is especially relevant for:
• college gymnasts and NCAA athletes
• Christian athletes navigating team dynamics
• women in sports seeking purpose beyond performance
• anyone learning to see competition as calling
Part of our Purpose Over Performance series exploring faith, identity, and calling in college athletics.

🎧 From Beam Boldly with Brooke Gleichowski,
Episode 2 — Rivalry and Faith ft. Creslyn Brose and Sharon Lee.

A faith-based sports podcast focused on college athlete mental health, faith, and purpose beyond the sport.

caption:
When volleyball disappeared, so did Brooke Bultema’s identity.

Covid took away tournaments, recruiting, and the ability to perform—leaving her with a question she couldn’t answer: Who am I if I can’t play? That season exposed how deeply her worth was tied to her sport and forced her to confront something she had never fully surrendered.

In the quiet, when everything was stripped away, Brooke encountered Jesus not just as a concept, but as her true identity.

🎧 Watch the full story in Episode 10 of The Filled Podcast with Brooke Bultema, former University of Kentucky volleyball player and current Louisville player.

athlete.bio: A tenacious force at the net, this Middle Blocker blends fierce determination with strategic finesse. Hailing from a small town, her leadership inspires teammates, while her playful spirit keeps the game lively.

caption:
Big Blue Nation, 

Thank you will never be enough. This place, these people, this commonwealth, will forever hold a special place in my heart. Leaving Kentucky was the hardest decision of my life. Not only because I was leaving a school I loved, but people that have forever changed my life for the better. From on the court, FCA, the classroom, and on the streets of campus, this place touched every aspect of my life in so many beautiful ways. 

The biggest thing that this process has taught me is that the Lord is FAITHFUL. We can trust Him whole heartedly with everything. Every road He leads us down He is faithful to see us to the very end. Every mountain and valley has its purpose, and it’s all for His glory. And living this way is the most fulfilling way to live life. 

I can’t wait to see what’s next and I am super grateful that Kentucky got to be a part of my journey. 

Much love, 
BB8💙

caption:
I’ve been putting off writing this post for so many reasons. It’s hard to believe how fast the past four years have gone, and I never thought the day would come when I’d take my college jersey off for the last time. Playing college volleyball has truly been a dream come true. Through every high and low, I wouldn’t change a single moment, because each one has shaped me into the person I am today.
 This past year, though, has been especially unforgettable. I gained a group of coaches and staff who quickly became my family. Teammates who turned into lifelong friends. They gave me a new spark and love for volleyball that I didn’t even know was possible. 
  To BBN, thank you for welcoming me with open arms and for continuing that support, especially over the past few days. I am beyond grateful for everything you do for this program and for me. While it’s incredibly hard to say goodbye, I’m excited for what’s next in my journey and my career.
